column4: Combined conservative regularization tests whether stable, diversified action trajectories improve OOS robustness.
Action-acceleration penalty reduces buy/sell oscillation without directly forcing low turnover.
Mild L1 turnover penalty reduces unnecessary rebalancing without suppressing useful adaptation.
Negative control: very strong penalties should expose inactive-policy false positives.
Stronger turnover penalty tests dose-response and detects whether turnover reduction becomes performance damage.
Mild concentration penalty reduces overfit concentrated bets without eliminating active allocation.
Mild turnover plus smoothness regularization improves action stability more reliably than either alone.
